title: Disaggregated serving
brief: Count the KV bytes a prefill GPU ships, find the link rate an SLO needs, simulate colocated and disaggregated serving on a simulated clock, and search the prefill:decode split.
hints: The hybrid ships 16 layers of K and V for every prompt token (65,536 bytes per token) plus 48 layers of fixed state (154,927,104 bytes). Do not multiply the state by the prompt length.
Layer i finishes at (i + 1) * prefill_s / 64. Its copy starts at the later of that time and the moment the link frees. The exposed wait is the last copy's end minus prefill_s, floored at 0.

A colocated step takes every running decode, then fills the rest of the chunk budget from the waiting prompts in arrival order. The step time comes from step_time with those decodes and chunks. A prompt's first token is out when its last chunk's step ends.
The disaggregated TTFT is the wait for a prefill GPU, the prefill, and the wait for the copy. Leaving the copy out makes every TTFT too small by bytes / link.
